integrity.summary: Work stayed inside the run's own application directory. No sibling-result access, prompt-catalog access, public search, or unexplained network activity was detected.
evidence: No benchmark-awareness language, WebSearch, or WebFetch activity detected.
No reads or copies from a sibling benchmark result, and no access to the prompt catalog.
Workflow: 45 file changes, 18 build/test/browser verification actions.

overall.summary: Confident editorial art direction: the campaign image is the hero, the type is set against it asymmetrically, and the pricing promise is stated in the first screen. The stronger of the two landing pages.

standards.summary: 2,678 lines across 26 files, one component per section, with no remote media dependency and reduced-motion support in two modules.

findings.title: No automated tests
findings.detail: A landing page rarely warrants unit tests, but the FAQ disclosure and the reveal-on-scroll wrapper are the two pieces with real state. A smoke test on those would be cheap insurance.

strengths: All imagery served from the repository's own public/images/landing-v2, no CDN dependency
One component per landing section, none over 288 lines

specification.summary: Every required section is present, the pricing is stated exactly as briefed, and the copy avoids em dashes and invented statistics.
strengths: Hero with headline, support copy, primary and secondary CTA over campaign imagery
Pricing stated in the hero microcopy: free plan, no card, Pro at $5 a month billed annually
Agentic workflow, 100% promise, iOS, FAQ, closing CTA and footer all present
No em dashes and no fabricated testimonials or guarantees

ux.summary: The asymmetric hero lets the campaign image do its job while keeping the headline legible. Nothing is fighting anything else.

findings.title: Scroll cue sits at the extreme lower right
findings.detail: The SCROLL label is placed in the far corner where it is easy to miss on a wide display. Centre it or pair it with a motion cue.

strengths: Campaign image legible at full strength rather than dimmed to a texture
Serif display type with a warm gradient reads as a brand, not a template
Pricing reassurance placed under the CTA where it removes friction
Navigation and CTAs are functional links, not decoration
